wordNotes.h430: The same word stands twice in verse 1: the one standing, and the ones being judged. Number comes from the verbs around it, not from the noun.

aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abimelech.title: Abimelech
abimelech.note: Gideon's son by a concubine. He killed almost all seventy of his brothers to clear his own way, which is most of what Judges has to say about him.

abiram.title: Abiram
abiram.about: Aaron's adversary living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiram.note: He and Dathan went in with Korah against Moses and Aaron. The ground opened and took him, his household and the rest of them down alive.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

ahimelech.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech.note: The priest at Nob. He helped David, who was fleeing Saul, without knowing it, and gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Once Doeg reported it, Saul had him and the rest of the priests at Nob massacred.

alamoth.title: Alamoth
alamoth.note: It literally means maidens, and it turns up in the temple records and in a psalm heading, probably marking a high part.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

aram-naharaim.title: Aram-naharaim
aram-naharaim.note: Aram of the two rivers, upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's relatives settled there, and the wives of Isaac and Jacob came from it.

aram-zobah.title: Aram-zobah
aram-zobah.note: An Aramean kingdom under its king Hadadezer. David beat it in a series of campaigns, pushed Israel's borders out, and brought home heavy tribute.

asaph.title: Asaph
asaph.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph.note: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

baal-peor.title: Baal-peor
baal-peor.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal-peor.note: Israel, nearly at the promised land, got drawn into worshipping this Moabite god through Moabite women. A plague followed, and it took Phinehas acting in zeal to stop it.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

baca.title: Baca
baca.note: In Psalm 84:6 the dry Valley of Baca turns into a place of springs for pilgrims heading to Jerusalem, and the name probably plays on balsam or mulberry trees.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

bath-sheba.title: Bath-sheba
bath-sheba.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
bath-sheba.note: She was Uriah the Hittite's wife. David saw her bathing, sent for her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away fighting in David's own army. The cover-up ended with Uriah's death in battle, arranged by David.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

chush-3.title: Chush
chush-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
chush-3.note: One of 3 men called Chush. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in Psalm.

dathan.title: Dathan
dathan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
dathan.note: He and Abiram joined Korah against Moses, and the ground opened under their tents and took them and their families.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

doeg.title: Doeg
doeg.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
doeg.note: Saul's chief herdsman, an Edomite, who told Saul that the priest Ahimelech had helped David. Saul's own men would not kill the priests of Nob. Doeg did it himself, eighty-five priests and the whole town with them.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

egypt-2.title: Egypt
egypt-2.note: Named 5 times, in 1 Chronicles and Psalm, and nowhere else.

en-dor.title: En-dor
en-dor.note: Home of the medium Saul went to in disguise the night before his last battle. It lay in Issachar's land, near where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera. Endur, southeast of Mount Tabor, keeps the name.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ethan.title: Ethan
ethan.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ethan.note: In 1 Kings Ethan is one of the wise men Solomon outdid, and Psalm 89 is credited to Ethan the Ezrahite, possibly the same man. The name also turns up among the singers of Chronicles.

ezrahite.title: Ezrahite
ezrahite.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ezrahite.note: What Ethan and Heman are called. Both were wise men, counted as sons of Zerah in Chronicles, and the headings of Psalms 89 and 88 name them as the authors.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gebal.title: Gebal
gebal.note: Byblos, to the Greeks, a Phoenician port north of Beirut. Ezekiel says its craftsmen caulked the ships of Tyre. The ruins gave up the Ahiram sarcophagus, carrying one of the earliest examples of the Phoenician alphabet.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gittith.title: Gittith
gittith.note: Three psalms carry it in their heading. It may be a tune, an instrument or a style, and the name points at Gath.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

hagarene.title: Hagarene
hagarene.about: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hagarene.note: They were nomads east of Gilead, beaten by Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh in a war Chronicles records.

heman-2.title: Heman
heman-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
heman-2.note: 1 Kings and Psalm name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

hermon.title: Hermon
hermon.note: On Israel's northern border, and the snowmelt off it gives the Psalms their picture of dew. It is near Caesarea Philippi, which makes it a likely site for Jesus's transfiguration.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

ishmaelite.title: Ishmaelite
ishmaelite.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmaelite.note: The Ishmaelites came from Abraham's son Ishmael and traded across the country south and east of Canaan. One of their caravans bought Joseph from his brothers and took him down to Egypt.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jabin.title: Jabin
jabin.note: King of Hazor, and master of Sisera, whom Deborah and Barak beat. A Psalm still asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as he dealt with Jabin.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jah.title: Jah
jah.note: A short, poetic form of Yahweh, God's covenant name. It turns up mostly in the Psalms, and it is the end of Hallelujah, "praise Yah".

jeduthun.title: Jeduthun
jeduthun.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
jeduthun.note: David put three chief musicians over temple worship, Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Several psalms carry Jeduthun's name in their headings.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave Absalom. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kadesh.title: Kadesh
kadesh.note: Kadesh-barnea, Israel's main camp in the wilderness of Zin. Moses sent the twelve spies from there, Miriam died there, and there he struck the rock and lost his way into Canaan. It is usually identified with Ain el-Qudeis or Ain el-Qudeirat, where a fortress of the Israelite period has been dug up.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

kishon.title: Kishon
kishon.note: It is a winter stream that drains the Jezreel Valley into the Mediterranean below Mount Carmel, and it floods fast. It swept away Sisera's chariots when Deborah and Barak fought the Canaanites, and in its valley Elijah had the prophets of Baal killed after the contest on Carmel.

korah.title: Korah
korah.about: Aaron's adversary living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
korah.note: A Levite who led a revolt against Moses and Aaron, with more than two hundred fifty leading Israelites behind him, all saying the whole community was holy and Moses had no special claim. The ground opened and took Korah and his family alive, and fire burned up the rest. Israel complained about it the very next day.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

lot.title: Lot
lot.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lot.note: Abraham's nephew, who came with him from Ur. When their herdsmen started fighting and they split, Lot took the green Jordan valley and ended up living by Sodom. Angels dragged him out before it burned, and his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt. Afterwards his two daughters got him drunk and had sons by him, the fathers of Moab and Ammon.

mahalath.title: Mahalath
mahalath.note: Two psalms are set upon Mahalath. What that means is not settled.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

maschil.title: Maschil
maschil.note: Thirteen psalms carry this word in their heading. It probably marks a contemplative psalm, or a skilfully made one.

massah.title: Massah
massah.note: "Testing." Near Rephidim the Israelites ran out of water, quarrelled with Moses and demanded a drink, testing God even as he tested them. The place was also called Meribah, and what happened there became shorthand for a hard heart, used as a warning in Psalm 95 and again in Hebrews 3.

melchizedek.title: Melchizedek
melchizedek.about: Priest living at the time of the Patriarchs
melchizedek.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High. He blessed Abraham and took a tenth of the spoils, and Genesis gives him no family, no birth and no death. Hebrews builds on that silence to explain how Jesus can be a priest without coming from Levi. Josephus reads the name as "the righteous king" and takes Salem for Jerusalem.

meribah.title: Meribah
meribah.note: "Quarrelling." Israel complained there was no water, and Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it. That cost him the promised land.

meribah-2.title: Meribah
meribah-2.note: The other Meribah, near Rephidim, from Israel's first complaint about water in Exodus 17. Moses' blessing in Deuteronomy and Psalm 95 both name it again.

mesech.title: Mesech
mesech.note: Japheth's son, and the people who came from him. The prophets pair Meshech again and again with Tubal as far-off, warlike nations of the north.

michtam.title: Michtam
michtam.note: Six psalms carry it in their heading. Whether it is musical or literary, nobody is sure.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

mizar.title: Mizar
mizar.note: A hill near Mount Hermon, beyond the Jordan, that the psalmist remembers in Psalm 42 while far from Jerusalem and longing to go back. Where exactly it stood is no longer known.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

oreb.title: Oreb
oreb.note: He was one of two Midianite commanders the men of Ephraim killed during Gideon's rout, and the rock where he died took his name.

palestina.title: Palestina
palestina.note: The King James word for Philistia, the Philistines' strip of coast along the Mediterranean.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas.title: Phinehas
phinehas.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phinehas.note: Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.

rahab-2.title: Rahab
rahab-2.note: Not the woman from Jericho. This Rahab is the sea monster the poets use for chaos, and by extension a nickname thrown at Egypt.

salem.title: Salem
salem.note: The old name for Jerusalem. Melchizedek was its king when he came out to bless Abraham, and Psalm 76 uses the name again for the city where God lives.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

seba-2.title: Seba
seba-2.note: He was a son of Cush, and his descendants are tied to a kingdom somewhere in Africa or Arabia. The Psalms have it bringing tribute.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

sheminith.title: Sheminith
sheminith.note: Meaning eighth, and a direction rather than a name. It sits in two psalm headings and in the record of temple worship.

shiggaion.title: Shiggaion
shiggaion.note: Psalm 7 carries it in the heading, and Habakkuk has the plural. It probably marks something irregular and worked up.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

sinai.title: Sinai
sinai.note: Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

sirion.title: Sirion
sirion.note: What the Sidonians called Mount Hermon. A psalm has Sirion and Lebanon skipping like a young wild ox at the voice of the Lord.

sisera.title: Sisera
sisera.about: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
sisera.note: He commanded the Canaanite army that held Israel down for twenty years, until Deborah and Barak beat it. Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman called Jael, who took him in and then killed him.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

zalmon.title: Zalmon
zalmon.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
zalmon.note: Two things. A wooded hill near Shechem, where Abimelech's men cut brushwood to burn the tower of Shechem, and Psalm 68 has snow on it. And Zalmon the Ahohite, one of David's mighty men.

zalmunna.title: Zalmunna
zalmunna.note: He and Zebah were the Midianite kings who had killed Gideon's brothers. Gideon chased them down and caught them, told his young son to kill them, and when the boy was too frightened, did it himself.

zebah.title: Zebah
zebah.note: Gideon's other Midianite king, caught with Zalmunna. Both had killed his brothers, and he executed them himself.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zeeb.title: Zeeb
zeeb.note: They named a winepress after him, because that is where the men of Ephraim killed him. He was one of two Midianite commanders caught in Gideon's rout.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

ziphim.title: Ziphim
ziphim.note: The people of Ziph, who twice gave David's hiding place away to Saul. Psalm 54 is headed with that betrayal.

zoan.title: Zoan
zoan.note: Tanis, to the Greeks, a city in the Nile delta that was once Egypt's capital. Numbers says it was built seven years after Hebron. The psalmist puts the plagues in the field of Zoan.
